lists.AI Context Optimization: Repositories focused on optimizing LLM context windows—compression, pruning, ordering, or budget management—belong here. This is not Agent Memory, RAG/GraphRAG, LLM Model Routing, or Inference Engines, which cover persistent memory, retrieval pipelines, routing, and model execution instead.
lists.AI Design Tools: AI-powered tools for generating or assisting design work, such as UI mockups, graphics, or assets, distinct from UI Design Tools (conventional, non-AI editors) and UI Frameworks. It is not general AI automation or agent skills.
lists.Agent Harness: Agent Harness covers repositories that implement runtime scaffolding for executing AI agents—control loops, tool invocation plumbing, sandboxing, and run/session orchestration—not reusable skills, tool-call schemas, memory stores, or general AI automation. Most likely confused with Agent Tool-call, Agent Skills, Agent Memory, Frameworks/libraries, and Automation (AI Powered).
lists.Agent Memory: Repositories about persistent or working memory for AI agents—storing, retrieving, and managing agent state/context—belong here. It may be confused with RAG/GraphRAG, AI Context Optimization, and Agent Harness, but generic retrieval, context compression, or agent orchestration frameworks do not belong.
lists.Agent Skills: Repositories providing reusable, agent-executable capabilities—skill libraries, prompt/tool bundles, or knowledge modules for AI agents—belong here. Confused with Agent Harness, Agent Tool-call, and Agent Memory; runtimes, function-calling plumbing, and persistent context do not belong.
lists.Agent Tool-call: Repositories for LLM agent tool/function calling—schemas, invocation, parsing, and execution of external tools—belong here. Confusable with Agent Harness, Agent Skills, and AI-Powered Automation; general agent frameworks, memory, skills, or workflow automation do not belong.
lists.Automation (AI Powered): AI-driven automation tools that connect apps, data, or workflows to execute tasks without manual steps. Excludes Automation (Non-ai first), Agent Harness, Agent Skills, and Business Tools (AI).
lists.Automation (Non-ai first): This List covers conventional, non-AI-first automation tools, scripts, schedulers, and workflows where AI is not the primary driver; AI-centric agents belong in Automation (AI Powered), not here. Do not confuse it with Database tools or Frameworks/libraries unless the repo's main purpose is general automation.
lists.Awesome Lists: This List is for meta awesome-list repositories: curated collections of links and resources, not the tools themselves. It is most likely confused with Frameworks/libraries and Programming Languages; individual frameworks, libraries, databases, agents, or business tools do not belong here.
lists.Backend Scaling: Backend Scaling covers repositories and tools for scaling server-side systems: load balancing, caching, queues, horizontal scaling, and backend performance. It is not Database tools, Frameworks/libraries, or Inference Engines, which address databases, general app libraries, or model serving rather than backend scalability.
lists.Business Tools (AI): This List contains AI-powered tools for business operations, productivity, analytics, or management. It differs from Business Tools (Non-AI), Automation (AI Powered), and AI Design Tools; non-AI business software, generic workflow automation, and design tools do not belong.
lists.Business Tools (Non-AI): Repositories offering non-AI software for business operations, finance, CRM, HR, or productivity. Excludes AI-powered business tools, automation-first projects, databases, frameworks, and WordPress.
lists.Database tools: Database tools covers general-purpose database utilities, clients, query, migration, and admin tooling across engines. It is most likely confused with SQLite, Frameworks/libraries, and Backend Scaling; SQLite-specific, general framework/library, or scaling repos do not belong here.
lists.Frameworks/libraries: Frameworks/libraries covers general-purpose software frameworks and libraries across languages, not domain-specific ones. It is most confused with UI Frameworks, Backend Scaling, and Inference Engines, which focus on narrow areas; Programming Languages, which are languages themselves, also do not belong.
lists.Inference Engines: Inference Engines covers repositories that implement or provide engines for executing model inference. It is likely confused with Local LLM tools, LLM Models, Frameworks/libraries, and LLM Model Routing, which cover runtimes/apps, model artifacts, general libraries, or routing rather than inference engines themselves.
lists.LLM Model Routing: Repositories for routing or selecting among multiple LLM models/providers based on cost, quality, latency, or task. Confusable with LLM Models and Inference Engines; model weights, serving engines, and generic AI automation do not belong.
lists.LLM Models: Repositories about large language models themselves—model releases, weights, architectures, and training or fine-tuning code—belong here. Not LLM Model Routing, Inference Engines, Local LLM tools, or agent/RAG frameworks; those cover routing, serving, local use, or applications rather than models.
lists.Local LLM tools: Repositories for tools that run, manage, or interface with large language models locally on user hardware, such as local chat UIs, desktop runners, or CLI helpers. Most likely confused with Inference Engines and LLM Models; exclude model weights, cloud/API-based AI automation, and routing or context-optimization tools.
lists.Programming Languages: Covers language design, compilers, interpreters, runtimes, and official toolchains; not frameworks/libraries, Typesafe-Jev, Database tools, or SQLite, which cover app scaffolding, typed tooling, and data storage.
lists.RAG/GraphRAG: Repositories implementing retrieval-augmented generation and graph-based retrieval pipelines: indexing, chunking, retrieval, graph construction, and querying. Not general vector databases, agent memory stores, or context optimizers, which fit Database tools, Agent Memory, or AI Context Optimization.
lists.SQLite: Repositories specifically about SQLite—its engine, extensions, bindings, or SQLite-focused tooling—belong here. Not general database tools, frameworks/libraries, or programming languages; those fit sibling Lists Database tools, Frameworks/libraries, and Programming Languages.
lists.Typesafe-Jev: Repositories implementing TypeSafe Jev, especially recursive choice over taxonomies and workarounds for its choice cap, like reachjalil/jev-tree in TypeScript. Do not confuse with Programming Languages or Frameworks/libraries; generic TypeScript, taxonomy, or classification projects without TypeSafe Jev do not belong.
lists.UI Design Tools: Repositories for UI design tools—interface design, prototyping, and visual editing—belong here. Most easily confused with AI Design Tools and UI Frameworks; exclude AI-powered design generators and frontend code frameworks/libraries.
lists.UI Frameworks: Repositories providing frontend or user-interface framework code, such as component libraries, rendering systems, and state management, belong here. Most likely confused with UI Design Tools and Frameworks/libraries; visual design tools and non-UI general-purpose libraries do not belong.
lists.Wordpress: This List covers the CMS ecosystem: core, plugins, themes, and tooling; it is currently empty, so scope is inferred from its title and siblings. Most likely confused with Frameworks/libraries or Automation (Non-ai first); general PHP frameworks, CMS-agnostic libraries, and unrelated site automation do not belong.
